title: Perf/accuracy contour synthesis for batch+cache config changes
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a systematic, reproducible process to map how combinations of batching and KV cache parameters move the performance-vs-quality surface for representative workloads. The primary output is a probabilistic contour map (surrogate model) that predicts latency/throughput and quality delta for unseen configs, plus a lightweight dashboard and alert rules that tie config deltas to likely quality regressions. Motivation: Recent config sweeps and autoscaling changes have produced non-obvious regressions where token-level optimizations (microbatch size, batch slack, cache TTL/merge policies) improved throughput at the expense of subtle quality shifts for specific slices (multi-turn recency, instruction-heavy prompts). We need tooling to: 1) quickly surface risky regions of config space, 2) recommend Pareto-safe configs, and 3) generate regression-alert thresholds when new model or config rolls occur.

Scope & non-goals: Scope covers CPU/GPU-hosted runtime parameters relevant to batching and KV cache (microbatch size, max batch, batch latency cap, prefix cache TTL, merge window, cache eviction policy flags). We will evaluate across a matrix of representative models (gpt-open-3B, opt-30B-quant, and an internal Llama-variant) and three workload archetypes (single-turn completion, multi-turn chat with long recency, instruction-following QA). Non-goal: model training changes or tokenizer redesigns — those are handled by model-onboarding tracks.

Methodology: 1) Workload construction: derive 6 canonical slices from production traces and synthetic adversarial prompts maintained in redwood-evals/workloads (edge_recency, prompt_churn, long_generation, high_repetition, safety-sensitive, structured-output). 2) Config sampling: use Latin Hypercube Sampling across continuous/ordinal params to pick ~120 candidate configs; include targeted grid points near current defaults for high-fidelity probing. 3) Execution harness: run parallel evaller pods (k8s job matrix) to collect: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, RPC error rate, memory peak, and quality metrics per-slice (BERTScore, semantic similarity via embed-similarity, end-task EM/F1 for QA slices, and a human-proxy acceptance score where available). 4) Surrogate fitting: train a Gaussian Process (or Tree-structured Parzen as fallback) per model+slice to predict latency and quality deltas with uncertainty estimates. 5) Pareto & risk surfaces: compute Pareto front for throughput vs quality loss and produce contour thresholds (safe/gray/risky). 6) Integration: push results to Console as a new "Config Surface" dashboard and add generated rules to the regression monitor (e.g., flag when a rollout decreases predicted quality beyond slice-specific threshold with >80% posterior probability).

Metrics/Success criteria: - Surrogate R^2 >= 0.7 on held-out config points for both latency and primary quality metric, or calibration diagnostics show uncertainty intervals cover observed deltas ~90% of the time. - Able to identify at least 3 previously-unknown risky config regions when run against last two months of production roll diffs. - Dashboard and alert PR merged; SRE oncall has a playbook entry referencing these surfaces. Deliverables: - Evaluation harness PR (repo: infra/evals/config-surface), - Notebook and reproducible pipeline for surrogate fitting, - Console dashboard prototype and a CI job that re-evaluates key configs on every release-candidate model or runtime change, - Regression monitor rules and runbook snippets.

Risks & mitigations: - Noise/variance in latency measurements: mitigate with replication per-config and bootstraped uncertainty. - Quality metric brittleness for certain slices: include human-in-the-loop checks on flagged regressions and add slice-specific conservative thresholds. - Cost/time: use staged sampling (coarse->refine) to reduce run count and leverage cached KV snapshots to avoid re-warming costs.

Timeline (2 sprints): Week 1: sampling design, harness skeleton, pick model+slice list. Week 2: run initial 40-config pilot, fit surrogate, iterate. Week 3: expand to full 120-config run, dashboard prototype, alert rule draft. Week 4: integrate with Console, add CI hook, docs and handover to SRE/Optimize. Expected blockers: test cluster GPU availability, embedding-quality pipeline quotas.

Notes & references: - Related tickets: ENG-40210 (canary rollout telemetry), ENG-62108 (kvcache safety margin audit) - Evaluation datasets: redwood-evals/workloads/config-surface-v1 - Early idea: incorporate multi-output GP to jointly model latency and quality covariance so we can compute posterior probability of violating quality at given latency gains.
